title: Reflexivity of the symplectic form
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, $n$ a natural number, and let $\omega$ be the bilinear form on $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$ given by $\omega(u,v) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$ for $u = (x,z)$ and $v = (x',z')$. Then $\omega$ is reflexive: for all $u, v \in V$, if $\omega(u,v) = 0$ then $\omega(v,u) = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: omega is the symplectic bilinear form on V = F_p^n × F_p^n
replaced: The bundled symplectic form $\mathrm{symB}$ is reflexive.
